title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
abstract: arXiv:2610.29211v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We prove that for every open $ U \subseteq \mathbb R^n $ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $\theta(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb R$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field.   Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. tldr: 该论文证明了任意 o-极小结构中可定义 $C^1$-势函数的每条梯度轨迹（无论收敛还是发散到无穷远）的球面投影长度有限（即总角运动有限且方向收敛），从而对无穷远处梯度猜想和可定义 Thom 梯度猜想给出了肯定的回答。
en_tdlr: The paper proves that every gradient trajectory of a definable C¹-potential—whether convergent or diverging to infinity—has finite spherical projection length (finite total angular motion with directional convergence), thereby affirmatively answering both the gradient conjecture at infinity and the definable Thom gradient conjecture.
